2607.03449.title: HiMe: Hierarchical Embodied Memory for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Control
2607.03449.paper_summary: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models excel at robotic manipulation but often struggle with non-Markovian tasks requiring long-term memory and reasoning due to their reliance on immediate observations. Existing solutions face a ''frequency-competence paradox,'' where stronger reasoning models are too slow for real-time control, while faster models lack sufficient reasoning capabilities. To resolve this architectural misalignment, we propose HiMe, a Hierarchical Embodied Memory framework that decouples embodied intelligence into a high-frequency Executor for execution, a Sentry for working memory, and a Planner for long-term strategy. We also introduce a dynamic knowledge system based on cross-modal semantic schemas and active management mechanisms, allowing robots to maintain memory plasticity through ''Add, Update, and Delete'' operations. This hierarchical design effectively balances the conflict between real-time execution and slow thinking planning, significantly improving success rates in long-horizon tasks. Experiments demonstrate that this approach not only outperforms flat memory baselines but also exhibits the novel ability to self-correct its internal knowledge based on human preferences.
2607.03449.paper_summary_zh: 當前的視覺-語言-行動 (VLA) 模型在機器人操作方面表現出色，但通常在需要長期記憶和推理的非馬可夫任務中掙扎，因為它們依賴於即時觀察。現有解決方案面臨著「頻率-能力悖論」，即更強的推理模型在實時控制中過於緩慢，而更快的模型則缺乏足夠的推理能力。為了解決這一架構不匹配的問題，我們提出了 HiMe，一個層次化的具身記憶框架，將具身智能解耦為高頻執行者用於執行、哨兵用於工作記憶，以及規劃者用於長期策略。我們還引入了一個基於跨模態語義架構和主動管理機制的動態知識系統，使機器人能夠通過「添加、更新和刪除」操作來保持記憶的可塑性。這種層次化設計有效地平衡了實時執行與緩慢思考規劃之間的衝突，顯著提高了長期任務的成功率。實驗表明，這種方法不僅超越了平面記憶基準，還展現了根據人類偏好自我修正內部知識的新能力。
